title: The Černý synchronizing-automaton conjecture
decision_reason: Source formulation, independent status corroboration, actual resolution searches and scope comparisons, full baseline screening, applied significance and separate adversarial self-review passed. Accepted draft awaits a 10–20-entry integration batch and prepublication refresh.

problem_fingerprint.domain: Finite nonempty state set and finite nonempty alphabet; total transition function
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Unknown initial state; same word must reset all states
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Every synchronizing n-state automaton admits a reset word of length at most (n-1)^2
problem_fingerprint.normalization: One input letter costs one time step
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Deterministic automaton; existential word bound, not a polynomial-time word-finding algorithm

statement_source_and_scope_match: Volkov §1.1 defines completeness and words; §1.2 gives exact bound. No restriction to two-letter, Eulerian or one-cluster automata.
proposed_statement_text: Let Q be a nonempty n-element set and Sigma a nonempty finite alphabet, with a total transition map delta: Q x Sigma -> Q extended by composition to words. Suppose some word sends every state to the same state. Must there be such a word with at most (n-1)^2 letters?
applied_significance: A reset word drives a finite-state device to a known state from any unknown initial state without observing the state. The bound would quantify the worst-case number of control inputs needed for this form of synchronization; it does not itself provide an efficient shortest-word algorithm.

hypothesis_comparison: Requires an original alphabet letter whose functional graph has exactly one directed cycle.
A general synchronizing automaton need not have such a letter.
Adding an arbitrary reset word as a new letter changes the letter-count cost and cannot transfer the bound.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.scope_relation: Does not establish the full candidate.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The general alphabet and automaton class remain uncovered.

hypothesis_comparison: Assumes the bound for strongly connected simple, quasi-simple and radical automata.
These hypotheses are not established universally in the paper; a one-cluster theorem does not cover these algebraically defined classes.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: Continuous Skolem asks zero reachability of a continuous-time exponential polynomial, not reset words for every state of a finite automaton.
Analytic small-time local controllability concerns differential control systems, not finite-state synchronization.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: Universal reset-word length is distinct from all existing control and reachability questions. Restricted automaton classes are not separately counted.

open_status_evidence_summary: Volkov and Szykuła explicitly leave the general conjecture open. Historical full-proof claims were checked against withdrawal/error evidence; the July 2026 theorem concerns only one-cluster automata.
independent_status_corroboration: Szykuła §2.1 Conjecture 1, August 2026, independently lists the full bound as open.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: The general bound reported by both surveys is (7/48 + 15625/798768)n^3 + o(n^3), approximately 0.1654 n^3, far from the conjectured quadratic bound.
